summary: Linn County, OR L-4 lookout house built on Grizzly Peak in 1934; removed or destroyed in 1965; no source describes remains today.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1965 per the FFLOS register and the Forest Lookouts page; firelookout.com says destroyed that year. No source describes remains.

events.note: April 1931: Grizzly Peak named as one of eleven new emergency lookout stations; telephone link planned
Removed per the FFLOS register and the Forest Lookouts page; firelookout.com says destroyed
Registered May 7, 2011 as US 959, OR 317; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: built in 1934 as an L-4 cab and removed in 1965
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, this L-4 cab was removed in 1965.

evidence.supports: about three miles southwest of Mount Jefferson
firelookout.com says the cab was destroyed in 1965
evidence.quote: This L-4 cab, built in 1934, was destroyed in 1965.

evidence.supports: Grizzly Peak one of eleven new emergency stations
evidence.quote: Grizzly Peak will be one of the eleven new emergency stations.

evidence.supports: post to be connected to telephone system the following year
evidence.quote: This post will be connected with the telephone system next year.

evidence.supports: lookout removed 1965 per Forest Lookouts page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The sources agree on the year, 1965: the FFLOS register and the Forest Lookouts page say the L-4 cab was removed; firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year. The story gives the year and notes the difference in how the lookout ended.

notes_for_editor: Built year (1934) agrees across all three listings. Removal year (1965) agrees across all three; the FFLOS register and the Forest Lookouts page say removed, firelookout.com says destroyed, and the story notes that. No staffing names or dates found for Grizzly Peak; one search and three page reads turned up none. Nothing found on what remains at the summit today or on current access. Lookout photo on firetower.org (1943) not checked for license; none added.
